summary: The existing Infectum appetite construction has -li for the hungry experiencer and a zero-marked food stimulus. The new Preterit rāgle has no overt stimulus; -le's analysis as agent or experiencer cannot be settled solely by spelling.
Sexual arousal is entered as 1b under desire, with one attestation. Its bodily onset is supported by axər and the contextual reply; no new idiom or prepositional government is inferred.
Keep rāgle's long-vowel spelling and the inherited base rəgle. Neither variation nor the l-ending establishes a new stem or a separate alignment pattern.
The reader's contrast between personal wanting in the sexual context and impersonal appetite overstates what the two verses establish; both can involve an l-coded experiencer.
Confirm rāgle's local vocalism and whether -le indexes a personal subject/agent or an experiencer of an impersonal desire predicate.
Do speakers conventionally use ryg for sexual arousal, or is the sexual reading supplied by context? Subsense 1b is explicitly based on a single attestation.
